notes: This is a corrected mathematical typescript headed - IV- 1102 -, with 1102 supplied by hand. The archive pencil foliation 18 at bottom left is recorded as a comment, not as the mathematical page number. No date or separate title is visible.

The page begins section (21.6.5). It describes the closed subscheme Y(D) of a positive divisor by its invertible ideal and a locally regular generator, and states the converse for a regular codimension-one immersion. This is a report of the page’s assertions; I did not independently establish the global correspondence.

The slanted note alongside the converse reads provisionally "devrait figurer dans 21.2. (sans hyp. noeth.)". It suggests moving the passage and dispensing with the noetherian hypothesis there. The first two words, hyp. and noeth. remain marked doubtful. The bracket physically runs beside the lines from est un sous-préschéma through Gamma(U,O_X).
A separate slanted underlined "réf !" asks for a reference alongside the paragraph on maximal points and codimension. It is not an insertion into the proposition below.

The numbered formula (21.6.5.1) defines cyc(D) by the local lengths of O_{Y(D),x} for codimension-one points, weighted by their closed singleton cycles. The prime-like stroke on the sum and the small point beside the subsequent Z are retained as uncertainties.

Proposition (21.6.6) states additivity of D to cyc(D) on positive divisors. Its proof reduces to lengths in A=O_{X,x} and the isomorphism tA/tt'A ≅ A/t'A. The page ends mid-sentence with restriction to an open U subset X.

The live comma after the struck hypothesis Si X est noethérien appears outside the cancellation boundary. I preserve it with a doubt mark, despite the resulting punctuation, instead of silently deleting it for grammar.

The first D has a faint high stroke while I_X(D) and Y(D) use D. This potential inconsistency prompted an ink recheck and remains a doubtful prime. The no-bar codim singleton is also preserved even though H supplied a closure bar.
The second cycle-group glyph has lower-case height. I mark z|Z in the proposition rather than normalize it to the expected capital; the confidence in the case distinction is low.

All typewritten text, underlines, handwritten symbols, inserted wording, deletion groups, both marginal notes, the drawn bracket and archive foliation were checked against the viewed images. There is no mathematical commutative diagram or separate geometric drawing on this page.

math_checks.claim: tA/tt'A is isomorphic to A/t'A when t is regular
math_checks.work: Consider the A-linear map A/t'A → tA/tt'A, [a] ↦ [ta]. It is well-defined and surjective. If ta belongs to tt'A, write ta=tt'b. Since t is a non-zero-divisor, a=t'b, proving injectivity. This checks the specific isomorphism used in the last sentence.
math_checks.limit: This does not prove that the relevant modules have finite length or establish the earlier geometry.

math_checks.work: Use the exact sequence 0 → tA/tt'A → A/tt'A → A/tA → 0 and the checked multiplication isomorphism. Assuming the lengths are finite, additivity of length gives the written identity. Both repeated plus signs at the line turn are physical continuation signs in the source, not two independent additions in this deduction.
math_checks.limit: Additivity of finite module length is used as a known fact, not reproved.

math_checks.claim: A point outside Y(D) has zero stalk of its structure sheaf, viewed on X
math_checks.work: Locally Y(D) is cut out by the principal ideal (t). Outside its support t becomes a unit, hence A/(t)=0. This confirms the particular zero-stalk assertion under the local model stated on the page.
math_checks.limit: No global theorem about codimension or maximal points was independently proved.

math_checks.claim: The local length sum defines an element of Z^1(X) and positive divisors correspond to regular codimension-one closed immersions
math_checks.work: These assertions and references (21.2.7), (19.1.4), (21.2.5) were transcribed. No other pages or referenced sections were consulted.
math_checks.limit: The full geometric statements, finiteness argument, and cited propositions were not independently checked.
